revision.summary: Initial diagrams from SPEC.md: system architecture, verify pipeline, verdict model

generation.focus: System components and dependency/data-flow edges for Ply per SPEC.md §3 (Toolchain) and §4 (Repository layout): the three crates, the external engines as subprocess dependencies, and the key artifacts. No code exists yet; nodes are planned and left unanchored (files: []).

__diagram__.text: Ply is glue + UX over existing checking engines, never a solver (§1). Three crates: ply-attrs (proc macros, §3), ply-core (config/model/extract/arch/engines/harness/diag modules, §4), ply-cli (cargo-ply binary, §4/§6). Engines run as subprocesses, version-detected at startup; a missing engine downgrades affected checks (W0110/engine-missing) but never fails the run (§3). No code exists yet — all nodes are planned and left unanchored.

attrs.text: Provides #[ply::requires]/#[ply::ensures]/#[ply::pure]/#[ply::allow]/#[ply::derived] and ply::unresolved!(id, note). requires/ensures re-emit the annotated function unchanged plus cfg_attr(kani, kani::requires/ensures) — the real function is instrumented, never a copy (D2, §3).

extract.text: trait Extractor + syn backend: item index, call graph, caps, contract harvest, anchors. syn does no name resolution or macro expansion, so item-tier facts are approximate — every unresolved call site is counted and reported, never silently dropped (D11, W0312, §5.3).

arch.text: Two tiers (D4): crate-tier from cargo metadata is exact and default-deny (errors A0401/A0405); item-tier from syn is approximate and advisory by default, upgraded to errors under a component's strict: true (A0402–A0407).

harness.text: Codegen: in-crate Kani proof modules (cfg(kani)-gated, sees private items), proptest suites under target/ply/fuzz/, and rendered ply_cex_* tests. Uses plain format-string templates (templates/), not a parser of our own (§4).

kani.text: Version pinned in ply.toml and recorded in every evidence fingerprint (D9, D14). stub_verified(g) is only used when g itself passed a Kani contract proof this run in the same crate; any weaker case verifies against an assumed contract and marks the caller conditional (D5, §5.5).

plylock.text: Committed. Per claim: item token-stream hash, merged contract text, callee contract hashes, engine name+version+flags, active features, target triple (D14). A verdict is stale when any part changed (W0302); cargo ply accept re-blesses fingerprints and refuses (E0303) nodes whose last run failed (§5.2).

envelope.text: { command, ply_version, root: <node tree §7>, diagnostics: [<Diagnostic>] }. Additive changes only after M3; tests/ui goldens are the contract (§8).

diag.text: One Diagnostic schema for all engines: code, severity, phase, engine, check, node_id, content_hash, span, counterexample, assumptions, fixes, open_item (§8). Adapters never pass engine stderr/stdout through raw — parsed, or X0901 with raw output attached.

generation.focus: What happens on `cargo ply verify`: config load + schema validation → anchor resolution + fingerprint/drift check → fact extraction → callees-first ordering → harness generation → engine run → result parsing → counterexample materialization → Diagnostic assembly → ledger aggregation, per SPEC.md §5.4–5.5 and §7–§8. No code exists yet; participants are planned modules/artifacts left unanchored (files: []).

edges.label: load + merge ply.yaml, validate vs schema (§5.1)
item index, call graph, caps, anchors
generate harness: cfg_attr(kani) contracts, stub_verified if callee proved (D2, D5)
write in-crate proof module / fuzz harness (§4)
render cex as #[test] when inputs construct (D7)
assemble Diagnostic: code, span, cex, assumptions, fixes (§8)

__diagram__.text: Verification is modular: Ply checks every function against its own contract, and checks callers against callees' contracts, never their bodies (§1 finding 3). Verification runs callees-before-callers over the call graph (§5.5). A missing engine downgrades the affected checks (W0110/engine-missing) without failing the run (§3).

kani.text: stub_verified(g) only when g passed its own Kani contract proof this run in the same crate; otherwise f verifies against g's assumed contract and f's verdict is marked conditional (W0511), listing the assumption (D5, §5.5).

lock.text: Fingerprint = item token-stream hash + merged contract text + callee contract hashes + engine name/version/flags + active features + target triple (D14). Mismatch on any part → status stale, diagnostic W0302.

cex.text: Kani playback data is always stored (exact, engine-version-bound). The ordinary #[test] rendering is added only when the inputs can be rendered as stable Rust source; otherwise the diagnostic says so (W0541) — inputs are never fabricated (D7).

ledger.text: Worst-of aggregation over evidence order violation < unclaimed < tested < fuzzed < bounded < proved (D6). Statuses (conditional, stale, weak-spec, unsupported, engine-missing, timeout, inconclusive) do not sit in that order — they propagate upward as flags and open-item counts alongside it.

generation.focus: The node tree workspace→components→fns (§7), the evidence order violation < unclaimed < tested < fuzzed < bounded < proved (D6), and the orthogonal statuses conditional/stale/weak-spec/unsupported/engine-missing/timeout/inconclusive (D6, §7). No code exists yet; modeled as a conceptual class diagram, left unanchored (files: []).

__diagram__.text: The model is a tree: workspace → components → nested components → fns (§7). Every node carries { id, kind, anchor, content_hash, verdict, statuses, worst_descendant, open_items }. Verdicts aggregate upward as worst-of over the evidence order (D6); statuses do not sit in that order — they propagate upward as flags and open-item counts alongside it (D6).

component.text: Components may nest (components: [...] with the same shape, §5.1) — omitted above as a self-loop for readability; a Component may contain further Components in addition to Fns.

node.text: node_id is the component path + item path only; content_hash (blake3) is a sibling field, never part of the id, so IDs survive edits (D10).

proved.text: Strongest evidence a function's passing checks can earn (§5.4c). A single failing check yields violation regardless of what else passed.
